title: Chronic and Acute Phloridzin Treatment Protocol
author: Jason Kim
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.xujfnun

steps.title: Chronic Phloridzin Treatment via Osmotic Pump
steps.instruction: Administer phloridzin chronically using a subcutaneous Alzet osmotic pump.

substeps.instruction: Anesthetize mice with an intraperitoneal injection of ketamine (100 mg/kg body weight) and xylazine (10 mg/kg body weight).
Shave hair at the incision site on the back.
Make an incision (~0.5 cm) between the scapulae using a sterilized scalpel.
Subcutaneously insert an Alzet mouse osmotic pump containing phloridzin (0.4 mg/kg body weight).
Suture or close the incision site using sterilized staples.
Administer ketoprofen to minimize pain and house mice individually.

steps.title: Alternative Chronic Phloridzin Treatment
steps.instruction: Administer phloridzin chronically via intraperitoneal injection.

substeps.instruction: Perform twice daily intraperitoneal injections at 0.4 mg/kg body weight.

steps.title: Acute Phloridzin Treatment Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the mice for acute intravenous infusion of phloridzin.

substeps.instruction: Perform survival surgery to establish a chronic indwelling catheter for intravenous infusion 5~6 days prior to the experiment (refer to M1023: Surgery-jugular vein cannulation).
Fast mice overnight (~15 hours) or for 5 hours prior to the start of the experiment.
Place the mouse in a rat-size restrainer with its tail tape-tethered at one end.

steps.title: Acute Phloridzin Infusion
steps.instruction: Infuse phloridzin intravenously to lower serum glucose levels in hyperglycemic, diabetic mice.

substeps.instruction: Expose and flush the intravenous catheter using saline solution.
Connect the catheter to the CMA Microdialysis infusion pump.
Intravenously infuse phloridzin at 100 μg/kg/min for 60~120 min.
